canonical_statement: The study formulates post-failure memory recovery as jointly correcting the answer and persistent state after diagnosed faulty memories have already influenced agent execution while retaining unaffected work.

The repair input consists of a user session, active memory store, failed execution trace, diagnosed faulty memories, available tools, and runtime provenance; the output is a corrected answer, repaired trace, and repaired active memory store.
Fault diagnosis is outside the method scope; the approach assumes diagnosed faulty memories are supplied by an upstream detector.
Dependency-guided rollback repair has five stages: dependency graph construction, affected-subgraph tracing, independent-support checking, rule-guided rollback planning, and selective replay.
The dependency graph is a directed heterogeneous graph whose nodes represent user inputs, typed execution steps, and persistent memory records.
Graph edges are instantiated deterministically from runtime provenance and encode initiate, cite, support, produce, delete, update, consolidate, supersede, derive, and temporal-chain relations.
Pure temporal chain edges are excluded from contamination propagation because later execution alone is not treated as evidence of dependency.
For each diagnosed faulty memory, the method identifies a provenance-based reachability seed and traces explicit downstream propagation dependencies no earlier than the seed time.
The raw affected candidate set is the union of the provenance seeds and nodes reachable from them through propagation edges.
A reachable candidate is preserved only when its complete content or decision has independent trusted support from an admissible source outside the diagnosed-fault and raw-affected sets.
Preserved affected candidates are not recursively reused to validate other affected candidates, preventing mutually dependent affected nodes from validating one another.
The rollback planner deletes diagnosed faulty memories and quarantines unsupported affected memory records while retaining independently supported memory state.
Unsupported affected trace nodes are invalidated so that their outputs cannot serve as evidence for later repaired computation.
The planner restricts replay to unsupported affected execution nodes that remain on a dependency path to the final answer after deleted and quarantined memories are severed.
The executable replay set is formed by taking the execution closure of answer-relevant affected nodes and the final-answer node, while safe prerequisites are reused as preserved context.

Selective replay first applies memory dispositions, then recomputes selected steps in original trace order under the repaired memory state while withholding invalidated claims until replacements are generated.
The final-answer node is always regenerated from the repaired trace, producing a fresh corrected answer alongside the repaired trace and memory store.

Rollback repairs agent-maintained memory and trace state but cannot undo irreversible external side effects; re-execution of side-effecting tools requires resettable, idempotent, or compensating interfaces.
The method presupposes instrumented runtime provenance; incomplete provenance can under-trace contamination and spurious edges can cause unnecessary invalidation.
The controlled benchmark contains 150 tool-use cases across shopping assistance, travel booking, and customer support.

population.label: Controlled benchmark tool-use cases across shopping, travel, and customer support

canonical_statement: The 150 controlled cases comprise 48 shopping cases, 49 travel cases, and 53 customer-support cases.
Primary fault strata in the controlled benchmark comprise 42 poisoned, 34 stale, 34 wrong-user, and 40 summary-drift cases.

population.label: Controlled benchmark cases by primary memory fault type

canonical_statement: Poisoned records contain adversarial or corrupted values.
Stale records survive a failed deletion, update, or consolidation.
Wrong-user records are associated with another user or context.
Summary-drift faults corrupt consolidation output.
A controlled case is retained only when fault injection changes the final answer and creates at least one downstream effect.

inclusion_criteria: Fault injection changes the final answer
Fault injection creates at least one downstream effect

canonical_statement: Among the 150 controlled tasks, 128 contain one diagnosed faulty memory and 22 contain two or three diagnosed faulty memories.

At repair time, methods receive only the faulty store and trace, diagnosed fault identifiers, user session, and tools; paired clean executions, expected repaired answers, benign-memory labels, and affected-node annotations are reserved for evaluation.
Recovery is success under the deterministic task oracle for the repaired final answer.

outcome.definition: Fraction of evaluated cases labeled successful by the task oracle

canonical_statement: Recurrence is the fraction of successfully recovered cases in which the same failure reappears when the last user input is rerun.

outcome.definition: Failure recurrence among recovered cases after rerunning the last user input

canonical_statement: Faulty-memory removal measures the fraction of diagnosed faulty memories that are no longer active after repair.
Benign-memory preservation measures the fraction of benign pre-repair active memories that remain active after repair.
Claim invalidation F1 micro-averages precision and recall over gold faulty-trace claim identifiers requiring invalidation or re-derivation versus claims predicted for invalidation or replay.
Replay ratio is the fraction of eligible trace steps replayed by the repair procedure.
LLM count is the average number of LLM calls used by the repair procedure per evaluated case, excluding original faulty execution, deterministic evaluation, and recurrence probing.

Main controlled-benchmark experiments use GPT-4o with temperature 0 and seed 42, with all methods sharing the same tool environment, task inputs, faulty memory store, failed trace, and diagnosed fault identifiers; results are from a single run.
Full memory reset removes all active memories before replaying the final user turn, eliminating potentially contaminated memory but also deleting benign personalization state.

Delete retrieved memories removes active memories referenced in the affected region and replays the final turn without independent-support checking, derived-memory cleanup, or answer-relevant rollback optimization.

MemAudit-style is adapted as a memory-deletion selector using consistency anomaly and counterfactual influence signals, with an oracle-assisted diagnostic fallback only when the audit candidate set is empty.
LLM-judge repair asks an LLM to predict a validated JSON rollback plan from compact failed-execution artifacts and executes valid plans with the same rollback executor as the proposed method.
AgentTrace-style adapts trace root-cause scoring to select a replay region but does not implement explicit persistent-memory cleanup.
On the controlled benchmark, dependency-guided rollback repair achieved recovery 0.853 versus 0.773 for LLM-judge repair and 0.607 for AgentTrace-style.
Controlled-benchmark recurrence for dependency-guided rollback repair was 0.266; it was lower than AgentTrace-style at 0.341 but higher than LLM-judge repair at 0.121.
Dependency-guided rollback repair removed all diagnosed faulty memories on the controlled benchmark, with faulty-memory removal 1.000.
Dependency-guided rollback repair preserved all benign memories on the controlled benchmark, with benign-memory preservation 1.000; full memory reset preserved 0.000.
Controlled-benchmark claim invalidation F1 for dependency-guided rollback repair was 0.566, below LLM-judge repair at 0.946 and AgentTrace-style at 0.853.
Controlled-benchmark replay ratio was 0.123 for dependency-guided rollback repair versus 0.217 for LLM-judge repair and 0.091 for AgentTrace-style.
Dependency-guided rollback repair used 5.70 LLM calls per controlled case versus 9.80 for LLM-judge repair and 4.69 for AgentTrace-style.
Removing the rollback planner reduced controlled-benchmark recovery from 0.853 to 0.713.

canonical_statement: On the 50-case adapted LongMemEval-V2 subset, dependency-guided rollback repair achieved recovery 0.680 versus 0.540 for AgentTrace-style and 0.260 for LLM-judge repair.
On the adapted subset, recurrence was 0.059 for dependency-guided rollback repair, 0.037 for AgentTrace-style, and 0.077 for LLM-judge repair.
Dependency-guided rollback repair removed all diagnosed faulty memories on the adapted subset, with faulty-memory removal 1.000.
Benign-memory preservation on the adapted subset was 0.993 for dependency-guided rollback repair versus 0.997 for AgentTrace-style and 0.983 for LLM-judge repair.
Claim invalidation F1 on the adapted subset was 0.669 for dependency-guided rollback repair, exceeding AgentTrace-style at 0.603 and LLM-judge repair at 0.369.
Replay ratio on the adapted subset was 0.179 for dependency-guided rollback repair versus 0.123 for AgentTrace-style and 0.244 for LLM-judge repair.
Dependency-guided rollback repair used 8.22 LLM calls per adapted case versus 6.98 for AgentTrace-style and 10.64 for LLM-judge repair.
Controlled-benchmark recovery for the proposed method varied by domain: 0.943 in customer support, 0.729 in shopping, and 0.878 in travel.
By primary fault type, proposed-method recovery was 0.810 for poisoned, 0.941 for stale, 0.706 for wrong-user, and 0.950 for summary-drift cases.
By primary fault type, proposed-method recurrence was 0.000 for poisoned, 0.781 for stale, 0.125 for wrong-user, and 0.158 for summary-drift cases.
Under Gemini-3.6-Flash, LLM-judge repair recovery was 0.740 versus 0.733 for the proposed method, while the proposed method had lower recurrence at 0.091 versus 0.108.
Under Qwen3.6-27B, proposed-method recovery was 0.660 versus 0.613 for LLM-judge repair and 0.487 for AgentTrace-style.
Repair-cost analysis reports 12,697.55 total tokens for the proposed method versus 28,175.28 for LLM-judge repair on the controlled benchmark.
Recovery was 0.852 for one-fault controlled cases and 0.824 for two-fault cases; the three-fault bucket had recovery 1.000 but contained only five cases.
Across benign-memory-store-size buckets, proposed-method recovery was non-monotonic: 0.889 for 0-5 memories, 0.778 for 6-8, 0.914 for 9-11, and 0.793 for at least 12.

In the travel wrong-user case, the method deleted the wrong-user root memory, remapped the contaminated active flight summary to a corrected memory, recovered ANA as the airline, and preserved unrelated travel memories.

canonical_statement: In the adapted multi-fault case, three poisoned memories reinforced the same wrong ServiceNow label at different abstraction levels; the proposed method deleted all three, replayed the answer-relevant path, regenerated consistent replacements, and recovered the corrected label.

canonical_statement: The adapted LongMemEval-V2 subset contains only 50 selected procedural/navigation-style cases that can be reliably converted to the repair schema and does not represent the full LongMemEval-V2 distribution.

The paper explicitly cautions that the drop in recovery from 85.3% on the controlled benchmark to 68.0% on the externally derived adapted subset indicates the controlled results are an upper bound rather than a deployment estimate.
All reported main experiments are single runs at temperature 0, so the paper does not report run-to-run uncertainty for the primary benchmark comparisons.

The authors conclude that dependency-guided rollback repair achieved the highest immediate recovery across both evaluations with a favorable recovery-cost trade-off, while controlled-set recurrence remains an open weakness.
